articles.title: Karnataka Minister Eshwar Khandre asks officials to blacklist Larsen & Toubro for ‘delaying’ works
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre has directed that Larsen & Toubro Limited be blacklisted for alleged slow progress of work in drinking water projects
Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre has directed that Larsen & Toubro Limited (L&T) be blacklisted for alleged slow progress of work in drinking water projects.

The direction came after the final notice issued to the company that is executing drinking water facilities to 388 rural habitations in Dharwad district, Kalghatgi town, and eight en route rural habitations of Saundatti taluk, Belagavi district from the Renukasagar reservoir (Navilutheertha dam).

Sources said that though the work was awarded on April 20, 2022, to be completed by October 19, 2024, the progress on site was very slow. The daily pipeline progress is also less than 500 m per day, sources said.

It is learnt that instruction had been issued to complete trial run of all 126 villages, which are not affected by the proposals submitted by the Forest Department, to be completed within December, 2026, and the company was instructed to submit detailed week-wise completion plan for pipe procurement, laying, hydro testing and trial run.

Sources said that the officials informed the Minister during a meeting that despite the instructions, pipes allegedly had not been purchased, adequate number of workers had not been deployed and work was progressing slow, and that progress report was not being submitted.

In response, the Minister asked officials to black list L& T and issue final notice to all contractors who were delaying implementation of work, especially at a time when the State was reeling under drought.

articles.title: MP alleges intelligence failure over Nanjangud drug racket
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mysuru-Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar has accused the Congress government of a serious intelligence failure following the alleged busting of an inter-State drug racket operating under the guise of a banana plantation in Nanjangud by the Keralam Police.

articles.title: Swachh Survekshan: Guntur wins ‘Super Swachh League’ award
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Guntur finishes third among cities with a population of three lakh to 10 lakh under the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 rankings
Guntur has won the ‘Super Swachh League’ award after finishing third among cities with a population of three lakh to 10 lakh under the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 rankings.

Guntur Municipal Corporation Commissioner K. Mayur Ashok received the award from President Droupadi Murmu at a ceremony held at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi on Wednesday, along with Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P. Narayana, Principal Secretary S. Suresh Kumar and APTIDCO Managing Director B. Sunil Kumar Reddy.
Andhra Pradesh has secured six national awards, emerging as the second-best performing State in the country.

Mr. Ashok attributed the achievement to the collective efforts of municipal officials, sanitation workers and public participation. He said several initiatives had been implemented to improve sanitation and scientific waste management in the city.

A waste-to-energy plant is operational, while a Letter of Award has been issued for establishing a new Bio-CBG plant to generate green energy from waste. The civic body has also introduced electric autos, compactors and modern sweeping machines to strengthen garbage collection, he said.
Scientific removal of legacy waste, the ‘Swarnandhra-Swachh Andhra’ programme and the 30-day ‘Operation Clean Sweep’ drive contributed to improving urban cleanliness, he said.
The Municipal Commissioner pledged to continue efforts to transform Guntur into a cleaner and better-maintained city.

articles.title: Recent repairs on OMR come undone
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Sholinganallur junction has a bad stretch of road that is riddled with potholes; portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have come apart

Portions of Rajiv Gandhi Salai and the Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road continue to have bad patches and potholes that make driving on these roads difficult. These are the sections where the Chennai Metro Rail works are under way.
V. Raman, a resident of Mettukuppam, said the worst spot was the Sholinganallur junction.

“I drive a van at times and many commuters like me have to slowdown at this spot. This leads to considerable slow down of traffic flow. It is worse during school hours with more vehicles on road. Service lanes are in a bad shape,” he said. The Sholinganallur junction has a particularly bad patch that is riddled with potholes. Repairs undertaken recently seem to have come undone, said Krishna Suresh, a resident of Karapakkam.

“A lot of small-sized blue metal have come loose from both the OMR and the Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road. At times, the stones hit vehicles. Pedestrians find it very difficult to walk due to damages along the road,” he said.
Co-founder of Federation of OMR Residents Associations Harsha Koda said that portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have come apart.
“The height of the road was unnecessarily increased. No study on rainwater flow was done before the re-laying, which is why it has led to flooding. We need an independent flood-risk study.”

The Sholinganallur junction has a bad stretch of road that is riddled with potholes; portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have come apart

Portions of Rajiv Gandhi Salai and the Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road continue to have bad patches and potholes that make driving on these roads difficult. These are the sections where the Chennai Metro Rail works are under way.

V. Raman, a resident of Mettukuppam, said the worst spot was the Sholinganallur junction.

“I drive a van at times and many commuters like me have to slowdown at this spot. This leads to considerable slow down of traffic flow. It is worse during school hours with more vehicles on road. Service lanes are in a bad shape,” he said. The Sholinganallur junction has a particularly bad patch that is riddled with potholes. Repairs undertaken recently seem to have come undone, said Krishna Suresh, a resident of Karapakkam.

“A lot of small-sized blue metal have come loose from both the OMR and the Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road. At times, the stones hit vehicles. Pedestrians find it very difficult to walk due to damages along the road,” he said.

Co-founder of Federation of OMR Residents Associations Harsha Koda said that portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have come apart.

“The height of the road was unnecessarily increased. No study on rainwater flow was done before the re-laying, which is why it has led to flooding. We need an independent flood-risk study.”

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Deadlines to the two rounds were last extended in September by about two months to November 15.

The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

The AMULET SOPHINITY system from Fujifilm uses a high-resolution detector with a pixel size of 50 microns, allowing detailed imaging of breast tissue, including tiny microcalcifications, which can sometimes be an early indicator of breast abnormalities.

Mammography uses low-dose X-rays to examine breast tissue and can help identify abnormalities that may not be detectable through physical examination. The new system has intelligent exposure control, which adjusts X-ray exposure according to breast composition while maintaining image quality. AI-based positioning support is designed to assist in accurate positioning and consistent image acquisition.

The equipment takes approximately five seconds for standard image acquisition and 12 seconds for high-resolution imaging. It also has features such as flexible positioning, intelligent breast compression and automatic decompression to help reduce discomfort during the examination.

Speaking at the launch, S. Subramanian, Chairman and Managing Director of V.S. Hospitals, said early detection was important in breast cancer care and that mammography played a key role in identifying breast abnormalities.
The hospital will offer free mammography screening to underprivileged people throughout November 2026. Those seeking to avail themselves of the screening can contact the hospital at 7448850500.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 11 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.
Editorial Context: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. articles.title: IT hubs see 82% commute by personal vehicles, just 2% use public transport
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As Cyberabad grapples with growing traffic congestion, an overwhelming 82% of commuter movement across its key IT hubs is accounted for by personal vehicles, while public transport contributes just around 2%, highlighting the region’s dependence on private modes of transport.

According to data presented by Cyberabad Police and the Society for Cyberabad Security Council (SCSC), traffic across 15 key IT-sector locations exceeds 2.5 million vehicles and people every day. The figures underline the scale of the mobility challenge in one of Hyderabad’s fastest-growing employment hubs, which has a resident population of around 3.5 million spread across approximately 637 sq. km, apart from a substantial daily commuter population travelling from other parts of the city.

With around six lakh IT and IT-enabled services (ITeS) employees represented by the corporates participating in a stakeholder interaction on Tuesday, Cyberabad Police are looking to bring companies on board to encourage a shift towards shared and sustainable commuting practices.

Director General of Police C.V. Anand stressed the need for public participation, corporate collaboration and sustained awareness campaigns to improve road discipline and traffic management. Highlighting the five pillars of traffic management, namely Education, Enforcement, Engineering, Emergency and Enablement, he said changing established commuting habits would require continuous outreach through schools, colleges, workplaces and local communities.

Cyberabad Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Sunpreet Singh and SCSC CEO Naved Alam Khan presented an overview of the traffic situation in Cyberabad and outlined the measures being undertaken to address congestion.

“In a first-of-its-kind initiative, we brought together real estate developers, including My Home Group, Google and other MNCs, urging them to take an active role in easing traffic congestion through measures such as staggered office timings, traffic management initiatives and greater participation in improving traffic flow,” said Mr Singh.

Officials also called upon companies to promote employee carpooling, increase the use of larger shared transport vehicles, introduce centralised shuttle services and synchronise hybrid work schedules. Improved parking management and incentives for employees using public transport were also highlighted as possible measures.

The authorities also unveiled the logo of ‘Cyberabad Moves’, a three-day exhibition and symposium scheduled to be held from November 26 to 28 at T-Hub. The event will bring together government departments, startups, civil society organisations, school students, corporate leaders and citizens to explore practical and technology-driven solutions to urban mobility challenges.

articles.title: World Wars and India’s sacrifice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: We owe it to ourselves to be honest with our past, just as we owe it to our armed forces to honour the sacrifices of those who went before them

On the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month, most Commonwealth and other allied nations fall silent for two minutes to honour the fallen of the two World Wars. Not so much in India: wreaths are laid in cantonments, but for most, this is just another day. India has an uneasy relationship with Remembrance Day. articles.title: Civil police officer injured in attack by detained man in Keralam’s Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The officer was injured after a man who had been detained on charge of creating public nuisance in the city allegedly bit on his hands while he was being taken in a police vehicle for medical examination

A civil police officer (CPO) attached to the Ernakulam North police station was injured after a man who had been detained on charge of creating public nuisance near the North overbridge bit on his hands when he was being taken in a police vehicle for medical examination, on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

This comes two days after another CPO who was on traffic duty at the High Court bus stand was injured after a recklessly driven private bus rammed him. The incident occurred after the officer stopped a row of vehicles for an ambulance to pass through.

The Ernakulam Central police have registered a case against Muhammed Iqbal, 25, of Sashthamkotta in Kollam who, while being reportedly under the influence of intoxicants, bit on the hands of the police officer named Ajith Paul. He was seated on the last row of the police vehicle, from where he jumped into the middle row seat and reportedly tried to force open the door as the vehicle reached the Ernakulam General Hospital.

The officer was injured as he attempted to overpower him. The detainee also reportedly used abusive words. The police charged him under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Section 121 (1) — voluntarily causing hurt to a public servant to deter him from discharging his duty and 296(b) — use of obscene words in a public place.

He was taken for medical examination after he reportedly turned unruly at the police station soon after he was detained. He allegedly continued to create unruly scenes at the station even after being brought back after medical examination, a video of which went viral. Following these, he was remanded in judicial custody.

articles.title: Gem Granites Veeramani’s daughter Archana moves Madras High Court alleging human rights violations by SIT
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: She claims to have been deboarded from a Singapore-bound airplane and picked up from the airport by the police without showing any summons, warrant, court order or Look Out Circular

Archana Veeramani, 49, the daughter of R. Veeramani, being investigated as the main accused in a series of child sexual abuse cases, approached the Madras High Court with a plea to order an investigation into the human rights violations allegedly perpetrated against her by the State police and also to quash the summons issued after forcibly making her deboard a Singapore-bound airplane on October 23, 2026.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan is expected to hear her plea on Wednesday (November 11, 2026). The High Court Registry had numbered her writ petition (criminal) subject to maintainability. In her affidavit, Ms. Veeramani said, her father had been arrayed as the prime accused in a case booked by the police under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act of 2012 and other laws.

She was not an accused in that case at least as on October 23, 2026 and no court had restrained her from undertaking foreign travel. Therefore, she had booked a flight from Chennai to Singapore on that day to visit her son and help him take medical treatment for his ailments. After she had boarded the plane at around 2 p.m. on October 23, the airline staff forcefully deboarded her without assigning any reason, the petitioner alleged.

Claiming that no summons, warrant, court order, Look Out Circular or any such document was provided to her, the petitioner said that she was picked up by the police personnel from the immigration area and taken to the office of a Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the POCSO case against her father who was the founder of Gem Granites and a well-known businessman.

Since she was suffering from multiple sclerosis, a chronic autoimmune condition that affects the central nervous system, for about 20 years, the petitioner said that she collapsed on the floor of the SIT office at about 5 p.m. and lost control over her bladder. All these events were video recorded by the police despite objections and she was shifted to a hospital for treatment only on the advice of her doctor friend, the petitioner added.

It was only after deboarding her from the plane, picking her up forcibly from the airport and detaining her at the SIT office for hours together, the police chose to serve summons upon her at 9 p.m. on October 23, 2026 asking her to appear for an inquiry regarding the POCSO case on October 25, 2026, she said and urged the court to quash the summons besides ordering return of her seized laptop, mobile phone and luggage.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan is expected to hear her plea on Wednesday (November 11, 2026). The High Court Registry had numbered her writ petition (criminal) subject to maintainability. In her affidavit, Ms. Veeramani said, her father had been arrayed as the prime accused in a case booked by the police under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act of 2012 and other laws.

She was not an accused in that case at least as on October 23, 2026 and no court had restrained her from undertaking foreign travel. Therefore, she had booked a flight from Chennai to Singapore on that day to visit her son and help him take medical treatment for his ailments. After she had boarded the plane at around 2 p.m. on October 23, the airline staff forcefully deboarded her without assigning any reason, the petitioner alleged.

Claiming that no summons, warrant, court order, Look Out Circular or any such document was provided to her, the petitioner said that she was picked up by the police personnel from the immigration area and taken to the office of a Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the POCSO case against her father who was the founder of Gem Granites and a well-known businessman.

Since she was suffering from multiple sclerosis, a chronic autoimmune condition that affects the central nervous system, for about 20 years, the petitioner said that she collapsed on the floor of the SIT office at about 5 p.m. and lost control over her bladder. All these events were video recorded by the police despite objections and she was shifted to a hospital for treatment only on the advice of her doctor friend, the petitioner added.

It was only after deboarding her from the plane, picking her up forcibly from the airport and detaining her at the SIT office for hours together, the police chose to serve summons upon her at 9 p.m. on October 23, 2026 asking her to appear for an inquiry regarding the POCSO case on October 25, 2026, she said and urged the court to quash the summons besides ordering return of her seized laptop, mobile phone and luggage.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu police step-up surveillance on habitual offenders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 443 accused persons arrested in Statewide drive against rowdyism
The Tamil Nadu police have arrested 443 accused persons involved in various crimes, including drug offences and violent crimes, across the State and enhanced vigil on habitual offenders.

In a two-day operation against rowdyism and organised crime, which was launched on Monday, the police conducted intensive checks at places frequented by persons with criminal antecedents. Police personnel checked the activities of more than 15,000 anti-social elements and thousands of vehicles as part of the operation, which resulted in the arrest of 443 suspects who were produced in local courts and remanded in judicial custody.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Director-General of Police and Head of the Police Force, Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, said the two-day operation was planned decisively to curb criminal activities, disrupt drug distribution networks, and reinforce absolute public order.

Police teams across Tamil Nadu systematically tracked and checked 8,626 listed rowdies. As many as 796 habitual offenders were placed under strict preventive surveillance. During the drive, 1,624 drug offenders were tracked and checked. 77 individuals actively involved in illicit drug sale were taken into custody.

To prevent retaliatory crimes and maintain public peace, Dr Aggarwal said the police stepped up surveillance on 2,924 accused individuals previously involved in murder and assault cases, including those recently released from prison. “This proactive supervision led to the registration of 163 fresh cases and the arrest of 167 violent offenders,” the DGP said.

He said drone patrolling was conducted to ensure the safety of residential neighbourhoods and commercial areas. The state police used drones effectively and clamped down on open-air public nuisance. The police also tracked and checked the activities of 1,057 criminals belonging to deep-rooted criminal syndicates.

Resolving long-standing judicial bottlenecks, law-enforcement teams successfully tracked down and executed 73 Non-Bailable Warrants (NBWs) against fleeing or non-compliant offenders during the two-day operation.

“The Tamil Nadu Police reiterates its uncompromising commitment to maintaining absolute Law and Order, ensuring community tranquillity, and protecting the citizens of the State. Strict, proactive surprise operations of this scale will continue to be deployed against any elements attempting to disrupt public peace,” Dr Aggarwal said.

articles.title: Strategic autonomy must guide India’s Starlink policy
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: India must balance Starlink’s benefits with national security and strategic autonomy

Recently, Elon Musk unleashed a volley of social media posts, accusing Indian “oligarchs” of impeding Starlink’s entry into India. The government rejected the accusation and clarified that all satellite operators must go through the same regulatory process. The ensuing public debate has centred on Mr. Musk, Mukesh Ambani, protectionism and telecom competition. All this obscures important questions of how much control India will have over Starlink once it operates here.

In its current form, Starlink is unlikely to replace fibre and mobile networks because they have almost opposite strengths. Fibre and mobile networks take time and money to set up, but can serve many people in one area. Starlink reaches remote places without towers or cables but is limited by how many users it can serve in one region. While fibre and mobile networks are optimised for density, Starlink is optimised for reach. Starlink has previously stopped taking new residential customers in areas where it ran out of capacity.

articles.title: Karnataka-registered doctors may be allowed to practise in Kasaragod: Keralam Health Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Keralam government has recommended to the State Medical Council that doctors registered with the Karnataka Medical Council be allowed to practise in Kasaragod, considering the district’s special circumstances, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has said.
The medical council is expected to take a favourable decision on the recommendation soon, the Minister said while inaugurating ‘Kayakalpam’, a public outreach programme of the Health Minister.

Government hospitals should have adequate number of doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and laboratory technicians, the Minister said, adding that additional posts had been sought. Their early sanction would considerably ease staff shortage in the district.
The extension of the tenure of National Health Mission employees in Kasaragod till March 31 was also an indication of the government’s commitment to the district, he said.

The Minister said that he would direct the authorities to convene a meeting of the Endosulfan cell soon. Periye in Kasaragod was among the four locations proposed by the government to the Centre for setting up an All India Institute of Medical Sciences, he said.

Instructions had been issued to make hostel facilities available at the Kasaragod Medical College within two months. The construction of a hostel for nursing students would begin within three months, he added.
The government would ensure the services of a forensic surgeon at the Kanhangad district hospital. A new building for the District Medical Office would be constructed at a cost of ₹4.8 crore.

articles.title: Bihar Cabinet hikes 3% DA for employees, pensioners
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Cabinet approved the “Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme”, under which, 2,100 female students may be provided benefits beginning from the current financial year

Bihar Cabinet on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) approved a 3% increase in the dearness allowance (DA) for its employees, pensioners and family pensioners getting revised salary or pension as per the 7th Pay Commission recommendations.
The decision would provide relief to the common people during the festive season of Chhath.

“The Cabinet has taken a decision to increase DA by 3% three per cent from the existing 60% to 63%. It will be payable with effect from July 01, 2026. The hiked DA will be payable to government employees, pensioners and family pensioners getting revised salary or pension as per the 7th Pay Commission recommendations,” Cabinet Secretariat Department’s Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) Arvind Kumar Chaudhary told reporters here in a post cabinet briefing.

Similarly, DA has also been hiked by 7% (from 262% to 269%) and 14% (from 483% to 497%) for drawing salary/pension under the 6th Central Pay Scale and the 5th Central Pay Scale, Mr. Chaudhary said, adding that the hiked DA payable with effect from July 01, 2026.

In reply to a query, ACS said that the decision would put additional burden of ₹1,080.33 crore to the State’s exchequer. He, however, said that the amount for 6th and 5th pay scale people is minuscule.
A total of 32 decisions were approved by the Cabinet chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.

The Cabinet also gave its nod to “Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme”. It will be launched to promote innovation, entrepreneurship, and startup culture among female students enrolled in higher educational institutions and to help transform their innovative ideas into viable business ventures.

Under the scheme, a maximum of 2,100 female students may be provided benefits beginning from the current financial year. The scheme shall be implemented over a period of four financial years, from 2026-27 to 2029-30. A sum of ₹88.20 crore has been approved for the purpose.

In order to encourage the participation of female students in the fields of higher education and research, the Cabinet approved “Chief Minister’s Girls’ Ph.D. Fellowship Scheme”. The scheme will be implemented over four financial years, from 2026–27 to 2029–30. A sum of ₹126 crore has been approved for the purpose.

The launch of the “Chief Minister’s Girls’ Ph.D. Fellowship Scheme” is expected to increase the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) of women in higher education and enable female students to avail themselves of the benefits of higher education

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh Cabinet clears policy frameworks to attract investments in AI, electronics, renewable energy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Directorate of Traffic Management and Road Safety to be set up at Mangalagiri; ₹31,387-crore green integrated AI data centre proposed by AM Intelligence at Amanam in Visakhapatnam district cleared

The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu at the Secretariat on Tuesday, approved a series of proposals aimed at attracting investments in artificial intelligence, electronics, renewable energy, pharmaceuticals and manufacturing, besides taking decisions on infrastructure, education and administration.

The Cabinet approved the Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) Policy 2026-31 and the Robotics and Physical AI Policy 2026-36. It also cleared amendments to the Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 2024-29. The Cabinet approved the establishment of a dedicated Directorate of Traffic Management and Road Safety under the supervision of the Director-General of Police (DGP), with its headquarters at Mangalagiri.

Among the major investment proposals, the Cabinet approved an investment of ₹31,387 crore by AM Intelligence for a 512 MW green integrated AI data centre at Amanam in Bheemunipatnam mandal of Visakhapatnam district. It also cleared a ₹4,000.20-crore Carbon Cosmo advanced materials manufacturing project at Naidupeta and land allotment to Dixon Technologies in Tirupati for an investment of ₹700 crore, sources said.

The Cabinet approved the allocation of about 25 acres to Reliance Industries for a gigascale AI data centre at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district. An Epack unit for manufacturing AI data centre equipment will be established at Rambilli in Anakapalli district with an investment of ₹570.20 crore, creating employment for 2,565 people.

The Hetero Group was granted 173.82 acres in Nakkapalli Bulk Drug Park for its pharmaceutical units. The Cabinet also approved a ₹236.92-crore expansion project of Ravali Spinners in West Godavari district, expected to provide employment to 1,569 people.

The Cabinet cleared a proposal to establish a 30-acre FICCI FLO industrial park exclusively for women entrepreneurs at Jaggayyapet in NTR district. An integrated footwear park spread over 56.82 acres in Annamayya district and an MSME park at Thamballapalle were also approved.

On the energy front, the Cabinet approved the establishment of compressed biogas plants in NTR, Prakasam and Vizianagaram districts and agreed to examine the feasibility of setting up nuclear power plants using Small Modular Reactor (SMR) technology as an alternative to thermal power.

It approved the transfer of 5.50 acres of APGENCO land to the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC) for a 15 MW waste-to-energy plant. A 30-year lease of 192.68 acres of Wakf land in Vajrakarur mandal in Anantapur district for a solar power project was also cleared.

Other decisions included allotment of five acres on lease to a Kendriya Vidyalaya at Shakamuru in the capital region, exemption from stamp duty and registration charges, and allotment of two acres for a Government Industrial Training Institute at Penukonda.

The Cabinet approved the creation of two posts, Principal Sannidhi Yadava and Sannidhi Yadava, at the Tirumala temple and a Chief Sthapathi post in the Endowments Department. It approved the withdrawal of earlier land allotments made to Websol Renewables and Metro Decorative at the Naidupeta Special Economic Zone.

articles.title: Bihar CM suspends 15 officers for negligence of duty
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nine officers of Revenue and Land Reforms Department (RLRD) four officers from the Public Health Engineering Department and one officer each from the Rural Development Department and the Urban Development Department have faced the action.

Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) suspended 15 officers with immediate effect for negligence and failure to ensure the quality resolution of applications under the ‘Sahyog’ (Assistance) Programme.
The action has been taken and departmental proceedings have also been initiated against them for failing to process applications in a timely manner,

Nine officers of Revenue and Land Reforms Department (RLRD), four officers from the Public Health Engineering Department and one officer each from the Rural Development Department and the Urban Development Department have faced the action.
The officers include Block Development Officers (BDOs) and Circle Officers (COs), assistance engineers and junior engineers.

“All officers and personnel must extend their full cooperation in the processing of applications. It is our duty to address everyone’s problems with sensitivity and promptness, and to ensure they receive justice,” Mr. Choudhary said while holding the ‘State-Level Sahyog Programme at Chief Minister’s Secretariat where 76 applications were received.

He further said that the government’s objective is to ensure a transparent, fair, and time-bound resolution to every citizen’s grievance. The ‘Sahyog’ camps are intended to address public concerns and ensure citizen satisfaction.

Mr. Choudhary has directed all District Magistrates, departmental secretaries, and officials within the Chief Minister’s Secretariat to go beyond merely reviewing the timeliness of the resolution of applications received through the ‘Sahyog’ portal; they must also conduct a thorough review of the quality of these resolutions.

The initiative, which was launched for the first time by Mr. Choudhary, is part of the state government’s ‘Ease of Living’ under the ambitious ‘Saat Nischay-3’ programme aimed at delivering services at citizens’ doorsteps.

At the time of launching the initiative in May 19, 2026, it was already mentioned that if a case is not resolved within 30 days of receiving the application, suspension and disciplinary action will be taken against the responsible officers. These camps are organised on the first and third Tuesdays of every month to address complaints related to block offices, police stations, and revenue offices.
Mr. Choudhary instructed officials to ensure that the grievances of the general public are addressed with complete clarity and transparency.

Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) suspended 15 officers with immediate effect for negligence and failure to ensure the quality resolution of applications under the ‘Sahyog’ (Assistance) Programme.

The action has been taken and departmental proceedings have also been initiated against them for failing to process applications in a timely manner,

Nine officers of Revenue and Land Reforms Department (RLRD), four officers from the Public Health Engineering Department and one officer each from the Rural Development Department and the Urban Development Department have faced the action.

Mr. Choudhary has directed all District Magistrates, departmental secretaries, and officials within the Chief Minister’s Secretariat to go beyond merely reviewing the timeliness of the resolution of applications received through the ‘Sahyog’ portal; they must also conduct a thorough review of the quality of these resolutions.

The initiative, which was launched for the first time by Mr. Choudhary, is part of the state government’s ‘Ease of Living’ under the ambitious ‘Saat Nischay-3’ programme aimed at delivering services at citizens’ doorsteps.

At the time of launching the initiative in May 19, 2026, it was already mentioned that if a case is not resolved within 30 days of receiving the application, suspension and disciplinary action will be taken against the responsible officers. articles.title: Producers welcome proposal for minimum sustainable price for tea
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tea Board of India has recommended a proposal to the Ministry of Commerce to implement minimum sustainable price (MSP) for tea. Several stake holders said that MSP is essential for long-term sustainability of the industry

Observing that a committee of Tea Board of India has recommended a proposal to implement minimum sustainable price for tea, several stakeholders of the tea industry on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) welcomed the proposal and said that such an initiative will help in increasing wages of tea garden workers and is essential for long term sustainability of the industry.

Representatives of different associations associated with the industry expressed apprehensions that with implementation of the Code on Wages, there will be a further increase in wage costs, and the financial viability of tea producers is likely to face additional challenges

“The tea industry is confronted with mounting cost pressures, while tea price realisations have remained relatively stagnant. A Minimum Sustainable Price framework is therefore essential to bridge the widening gap between production costs and market realisations and to ensure the long-term sustainability of the industry,” said C. K Dhanuka, Chairman, Dhunseri Tea and Industries. Mr. Dhanuka added that a minimum sustainable price will help bring realisations in line with costs, so that the industry can accommodate wage revisions, protect employment and the competitiveness of Indian tea.
The proposal of implementing minimum sustainable price for tea have been made to Ministry of Commerce, which is yet to take a decision on the proposal, the stakeholders of tea industry said.

Suneel Singh Sikand, chairman of Indian Tea Association (ITA) called the recommendation for a minimum sustainable price is an important policy intervention towards addressing the structural challenges confronting the Indian tea industry.

“Ensuring remunerative returns to producers is critical to sustaining operations, facilitating investment in re-plantation and productivity enhancement and securing the industry’s long-term sustainability,” Mr. Sikand said.

Hemanta Bangur, former president of ITA said that the industry has failed to uplift the workforce and something is fundamentally wrong with the industry as the balance sheet of most of the tea growers is in the red.
“The market is dysfunctional and there is no level playing field. If market forces are left to determine the fate of industry, it will bring about the demise of tea gardens,” he said.
The Tea Industry employs millions of workers in about 270 large tea gardens and hundreds of small tea gardens across the State. The daily wage for a tea garden worker in West Bengal is ₹250 per day.

Representatives of Indian Tea Association (ITA), Tea Association of India (TAI), United Planters’ Association of Southern India (UPASI), Confederation of Indian Small Tea Growers Associations (CISTA) and Federation of Indian Tea Manufacturers Association (FITMA) issued a press statement on the stagnation in the prices over the past several years

articles.title: Bombay High Court declines request for hearing each day in quota petitions for Maratha reservation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bombay High Court on November 5 declined a request to hear each day a set of petitions on a quota of 10% for Marathas in education and service under the State. The court said hearing will continue on November 27. The document in the case is PIL 30 of 2024, Bhausaheb Bhujangrao Pawar vs State of Maharashtra.

A Bench of Justices Makarand Karnik, Nijamoodin Jamadar and Sandeep Marne passed the order. The Bench said it considered the request. It said efforts were being made to give priority to the PIL and matters that relate to it. It said a session for hearing was being assigned at intervals after taking into account work load from assignments. It said the matters were being heard at intervals. It said it would not accede to the request.

The Bench was constituted in September and has heard the matter four times since September 18, 2026. It has heard submissions from advocate Arvind Datar for a petitioner who challenges the quota. It is hearing petitioners.

The legislature passed the Act on February 20, 2024, and it was subsequently notified on February 26, 2024. The Act rests on a report of the commission under Justice Sunil Shukre. The report cited circumstances and situations as reason to grant reservation to Marathas beyond the 50% limit.

A petitioner moved the Bombay High Court against the SEBC Act, 2018, enacted by the government under Devendra Fadnavis. That law gave Marathas 16% reservation in employment under the State and in education. The High Court upheld the law in June 2019. It held that justification did not exist for the 16% quota and reduced it to 12% in education and 13% in employment under the State. Patil and others challenged that verdict in the Supreme Court. In May 2021, a Bench of the Supreme Court struck down the SEBC Act, 2018. It held that no circumstances justified reservation for Marathas beyond the 50% ceiling set by the 1992 Indra Sawhney judgment. The Supreme Court also questioned the data in support of backwardness of Marathas. The government filed a review petition. The Supreme Court rejected it in April 2023. A petition for relief after review is before the Supreme Court.

📰 Bombay High Court declines request for hearing each day in quota petitions for Maratha reservation

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The Bombay High Court on November 5 declined a request to hear each day a set of petitions on a quota of 10% for Marathas in education and service under the State. The court said hearing will continue on November 27. The document in the case is PIL 30 of 2024, Bhausaheb Bhujangrao Pawar vs State of Maharashtra.

A Bench of Justices Makarand Karnik, Nijamoodin Jamadar and Sandeep Marne passed the order. The Bench said it considered the request. It said efforts were being made to give priority to the PIL and matters that relate to it. It said a session for hearing was being assigned at intervals after taking into account work load from assignments. It said the matters were being heard at intervals. It said it would not accede to the request.

The Bench was constituted in September and has heard the matter four times since September 18, 2026. It has heard submissions from advocate Arvind Datar for a petitioner who challenges the quota. It is hearing petitioners.

The legislature passed the Act on February 20, 2024, and it was subsequently notified on February 26, 2024. The Act rests on a report of the commission under Justice Sunil Shukre. The report cited circumstances and situations as reason to grant reservation to Marathas beyond the 50% limit.

A petitioner moved the Bombay High Court against the SEBC Act, 2018, enacted by the government under Devendra Fadnavis. That law gave Marathas 16% reservation in employment under the State and in education. The High Court upheld the law in June 2019. It held that justification did not exist for the 16% quota and reduced it to 12% in education and 13% in employment under the State. Patil and others challenged that verdict in the Supreme Court. In May 2021, a Bench of the Supreme Court struck down the SEBC Act, 2018. It held that no circumstances justified reservation for Marathas beyond the 50% ceiling set by the 1992 Indra Sawhney judgment. The Supreme Court also questioned the data in support of backwardness of Marathas. The government filed a review petition. The Supreme Court rejected it in April 2023. A petition for relief after review is before the Supreme Court.

articles.title: U.S. Republicans derail bid to impeach Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee; this halts the immediate impeachment drive but does not prevent Democrats from reviving the effort after taking control of Congress in January

Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) blocked an effort to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war , handing President Donald Trump a victory days after his party's crushing midterm election defeat.

The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively derailing a planned vote on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) on whether to bring formal charges against the embattled Pentagon chief.
The resolution was introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, a Trump critic who was the only member of his party to oppose the procedural maneuver, according to U.S. media.
ALSO WATCH What are the impeachment charges against Pete Hegseth? | The Hindu Explains

The impeachment drive had threatened to deepen Mr. Trump's troubles after Democrats swept last week's midterms, with anger at the sputtering Iran war and soaring fuel prices helping drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans.
Republicans still hold a narrow House majority until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. And 11 Democrats missed the vote.
Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, in a post on X, hailed the vote as a "TOTAL VICTORY!"
"We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest."
Mr. Hegseth earlier on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) dismissed the impeachment effort as a "farce" and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under Mr. Trump.
"It's a farce, and it's a stunt, and everybody knows it," he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the accusations "slander" and "sabotage."

British authorities arrested a member of the U.S. Army on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) on allegations of spying for Russia. The 41 year old man, who has not been named, was arrested in Gloucestershire.
“The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing,” said Vicki Evans, a senior officer with U.K. Counterterrorism Policing.

“This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies,” FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement.

“While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message — this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners,” he added.
The soldier was based at Imjin Barracks, the headquarters of NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, as per a report in the BBC ..

articles.title: Pranab Mukherjee hinted at desire to become PM, ‘shocked’ me, writes Sonia Gandhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In her memoir, former Congress president recalls 2010 conversation; Pranab Mukherjee’s daughter Sharmistha asks what there was to be shocked about, says it is not a crime to be ambitious

Former President Pranab Mukherjee had “shocked” Sonia Gandhi by hinting at his “long-held desire” to become Prime Minister during a conversation with her in 2010, suggesting that perhaps it was time for a “change at the top”, the former Congress president has written in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love .
The book, published by HarperCollins, was made available in bookstores on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), but the official launch is likely to take place on November 16.

Mukherjee, then a senior member of the Manmohan Singh Cabinet, had developed serious differences with the then Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. He would sometimes stay back for conversations with Ms. Gandhi after meetings of the Congress Strategy Group, which was set up to discuss parliamentary business.

“On one occasion, in 2010, I think after expressing his frustration, he shocked me with the suggestion that perhaps it was time for a change at the top, which I understood as a hint of his long-held desire to become Prime Minister,” she wrote.
“I gently changed the subject, and though he may have been disappointed, he never made me feel he held it against me,” she added.

The late Mukherjee, who had served in Indira Gandhi’s Cabinet in the 1970s, was part of a core group that met weekly with Dr. Singh to coordinate the functioning of the government and the party. Other members included Arjun Singh, A.K. Antony and Ahmed Patel.
Ms. Gandhi says she often called on Mukherjee after he became President in 2012, largely to converse with the “erudite and knowledgeable politician that he always remained”.
Hitting back at Ms. Gandhi, Sharmistha Mukherjee, the late President’s daughter, said it was not a crime to be ambitious.
“What’s there to be shocked about?” she asked in a post on X in response to Ms. Gandhi’s remarks.

“Is it a crime to be ambitious, especially when that ‘ambition’ was supported by decades of experience in politics and governance, hard work and a brilliant mind? Once, when asked by me whether he wanted to become PM, he very candidly answered that ‘any politician worth his salt has this ambition’,” she wrote.

articles.title: After Bangladesh rules out passport for Hasina, India says ‘travel document’ needed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal described the passport’s requirement for extradition as a “technical issue” and said, “Obviously, for the travel of people, you need a travel document”

A day after the Acting Foreign Minister of Bangladesh, Humayun Kabir, stressed that Dhaka would not issue a passport to deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and insisted on getting her extradited from India under an “acceptable prisoner exchange”, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that a “travel document” was needed for international travel.

“Extradition of former Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina is a legal matter and it will be dealt with accordingly,” said Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal in response to a question about Ms. Hasina’s presence in India. He described the passport’s requirement for extradition as a “technical issue” and said, “Obviously, for the travel of people, you need a travel document.”
Officials said Ms. Hasina can be extradited either on a Bangladeshi passport or an Emergency Certificate that would prove that she has Bangladeshi citizenship.

On Monday (November 9, 2026), Mr. Kabir cited the extradition treaty between India and Bangladesh, which was signed during the Hasina era in 2013, and said, “Bangladesh will not issue a passport to any terrorist; there is no provision for such an action. Bangladesh will seek the return of Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner exchange process.”

An official dealing with the matter told The Hindu on Monday (November 9, 2026) that a passport was required for extradition. The deposed Prime Minister has sought a new passport and a national identity document through a London-based law firm that has written to the Bangladesh government.

Bangladesh has a history of leaders going into exile or being imprisoned for long periods after returning. Current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was in exile for nearly 17 years before he returned from the United Kingdom on December 25, 2025.
On August 5, 2026, Ms. Hasina had announced at a virtual press conference that she would return to Bangladesh in December this year.

Over the past few days, the law and order situation has deteriorated across Bangladesh, with incidents of violence, looting, and arson being reported. On Tuesday (November 10, 2026), Jamaat-e-Islami and the National Citizen Party, which are in the Opposition, accused the government of failing to maintain law and order.

Leader of the Opposition, Shafiqur Rahman, said the country’s Home Ministry has failed to contain the situation. “Even the Army Golf Club has now witnessed cocktail explosions. Similar incidents have occurred in front of the Special Branch headquarters, at police station gates, and at Dhaka University, where explosions have taken place for three consecutive days. Two people were injured there,” he said.

“Extradition of former Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina is a legal matter and it will be dealt with accordingly,” said Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal in response to a question about Ms. Hasina’s presence in India. Officials said Ms. Hasina can be extradited either on a Bangladeshi passport or an Emergency Certificate that would prove that she has Bangladeshi citizenship.

On Monday (November 9, 2026), Mr. Kabir cited the extradition treaty between India and Bangladesh, which was signed during the Hasina era in 2013, and said, “Bangladesh will not issue a passport to any terrorist; there is no provision for such an action. Bangladesh will seek the return of Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner exchange process.”

An official dealing with the matter told The Hindu on Monday (November 9, 2026) that a passport was required for extradition. The deposed Prime Minister has sought a new passport and a national identity document through a London-based law firm that has written to the Bangladesh government.

Bangladesh has a history of leaders going into exile or being imprisoned for long periods after returning. Current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was in exile for nearly 17 years before he returned from the United Kingdom on December 25, 2025.

On August 5, 2026, Ms. Hasina had announced at a virtual press conference that she would return to Bangladesh in December this year.

articles.title: U.S. House Oversight Committee criticises Trump administration over release of Epstein records
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The 137-page report, released by the GOP-controlled committee, comes nearly a year after Congress passed and President Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act

The Republican-led House Oversight Committee slammed the Trump administration on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) for botching the public release of millions of pages of records relating to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.

In a report scrutinising the government’s handling of criminal investigations of Epstein and his longtime confidant Ghislaine Maxwell, the committee faulted President Donald Trump and the Justice Department for reneging on a promise to open the files, which led Congress to pass a law forcing their release.

After Congress stepped in, the administration missed disclosure deadlines and concealed names of alleged co-conspirators while failing to adequately protect victims, “including through deficient redactions that exposed their sensitive information,” the report said.

The 137-page report, released by the GOP-controlled committee, comes nearly a year after Congress passed and Mr. Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which requires the Justice Department to publicly disclose records relating to the late sex offender, many of which were previously confidential. The report also comes on the heels of last week’s midterm elections, when Republicans suffered heavy House losses in failing to hold their majority after a campaign where the release of government records related to Epstein became a recurring campaign issue.

“The Trump administration has repeatedly committed to releasing Epstein-related files,” the report said. “However, multiple shortcomings related to releasing documents and failures to adequately communicate about those releases plagued the DOJ’s efforts.”

Democrats used the Trump administration’s handling of the files to accuse Republicans of protecting the wealthy and well-connected, suggesting Trump’s past relationship with Epstein exposed him to potential unethical activity. The report stated, “Trump’s lack of involvement is confirmed by numerous lines of testimony in interviews or depositions with various individuals.”

The Justice Department released the bulk of the so-called Epstein files in December and January. In all, more than 3 million pages of documents were disclosed, along with more than 2,000 videos and 180,000 images. Then-Attorney General Pam Bondi’s handling of the Epstein files contributed to her firing in April.

The records included documents concerning Epstein’s famous associates, including Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, formerly known as Britain’s Prince Andrew, and email correspondence between Epstein and Elon Musk and other prominent contacts from across the political spectrum.

More than 350 different ads mentioning Epstein aired since Labour Day for Republican and Democratic candidates running in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. Ads from Democratic-aligned groups claimed Republican candidates voted against releasing the Epstein files, while candidates from both parties accused each other of taking donations from associates of the convicted sex offender.

The report also examined how federal authorities investigated Epstein nearly two decades ago but failed to bring charges after multiple underage girls told police and the FBI that they had been paid to give Epstein sexualised massages.

articles.title: Trump ally Jim Jordan elected U.S. House Republican leader after midterm election rout
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Ohio Congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress

Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected leader of the Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), defeating fellow conservative Steve Scalise as the party reckons with a crushing midterm election defeat.

Mr. Jordan, the combative chairman of the House Judiciary Committee, beat the current majority leader by 106 votes to 73 in a secret ballot, U.S. media reported, putting him in charge of the party's opposition to the incoming Democratic majority.
The Ohio congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress in last week's elections.
Senate Republicans meanwhile reelected John Thune as their leader, retaining their existing leadership team despite demands from conservatives for a reckoning over the election losses.
Mr. Jordan, a founding member of the hard-right House Freedom Caucus, had pitched himself as the fighter Republicans need to confront Democrats during the final two years of Trump's presidency.
His victory represented a rejection of the party's established leadership, with Mr. Scalise having served in senior Republican positions for more than a decade.
Both men are staunch Trump allies, but the president declined to endorse either candidate.
The contest was a rematch of their 2023 battle for the speakership following the ouster of Kevin McCarthy.

Mr. Scalise initially won the Republican nomination but withdrew after failing to secure sufficient support, while Mr. Jordan subsequently lost three votes on the House floor before Mr. Johnson emerged as a compromise candidate.

Mr. Jordan, a former champion wrestler who has represented Ohio in Congress since 2007, built his reputation as a political brawler and fierce critic of the Republican establishment. Former speaker John Boehner once branded him a "legislative terrorist" for his uncompromising tactics.
