articles.title: Tamil Nadu may approach Supreme Court seeking greater powers for Cauvery Water Management Authority
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State wants the Authority to be modelled along the lines of the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB)

Frustrated that the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) does not have the power to enforce its orders, Tamil Nadu is contemplating approaching the Supreme Court with a prayer that the Authority be given teeth.
It wants the Authority to be modelled along the lines of the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), a case of which has been mentioned in the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal’s report (Volume V).

Established in October 1967, the BBMB is engaged in the regulation of the supply of water and electricity from Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects to Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi, and Chandigarh. The CWMA chairperson Saumitra Kumar Haldar, too, in an interaction with The Hindu in August , referred to the Tribunal’s recommendation and explained that the Board, with the chief being appointed by the Union government, “owns, operates, manages, and regulates” the projects. “They [the BBMB] take joint decisions regarding how much water is to be given and what the scheduling will be. Everything is planned,” Mr. Haldar had said.

Tamil Nadu has been complaining that despite the quantities of water release stipulated by the CWMA in the last three-odd months being inadequate and lower than the proportionate share, the upper riparian State of Karnataka has not provided water, as per the mandated releases. Of the seven spells of the 15-day water release ordered by the Authority since July 29 , Karnataka has not complied with the release in five spells, even though, cumulatively, Tamil Nadu realised about 5,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs) higher than the total figure of 5.71 lakh cusecs, according to a persual of the data measured at Biligundulu on the inter-State border of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

As per the data available with the Central Water Commission, four reservoirs of Karnataka (Krishnaraja Sagara, Kabini, Hemavathi, and Harangi) registered a net cumulative inflow of about 132 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft) during the period of June 1 to November 4, marking a shortfall of around 54%. The 30-year-long average net inflow was around 288 tmc ft. If the same shortfall is to be applied in the case of Tamil Nadu, the realisation should have been around 67 tmc ft between June 1 and November 4 against the quantum of approximately 145 tmc ft in a normal year. But Biligundulu received 53.43 tmc ft only with a shortfall of around 13 tmc ft. The Authority, however, has not asked Karnataka to clear the backlog, which, according to the calculations of Tamil Nadu, comes to nearly 17 tmc ft.

A senior government official says that even when the State had approached the Supreme Court seeking its intervention, the latter’s response had been to tell the former to go to the Authority. But the CWMA’s orders had not been implemented properly. “Besides, the Authority has not been able to enforce the directions. This is why we are mulling over the option of approaching the Court with this prayer,” the official adds.

articles.title: Periyar Arivulagam book purchase row: DVAC launches probe in Tamil Nadu libraries
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The issue was flagged by award-winning Tamil writer Perumal Murugan who visited the library in Coimbatore recently and pointed to issues relating to price, quality and authenticity of content in some books.

The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has launched a detailed inquiry into allegations of serious financial irregularities at Anna Centenary Library in Chennai and Periyar Arivulagam library at Coimbatore .

DVAC officers perused records in both the libraries on Monday (November 9, 2026) and Tuesday (November 10) after registering the detailed inquiry which followed a statement made by Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Rajmohan alleging that irregularities took place during the erstwhile DMK regime in the purchase of books for the newly-launched Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore.

Amidst allegations that books with AI-generated content and factual mistakes were purchased at inflated rates, DVAC officers made enquiries with the library staff and took copies of certain records in both the libraries for investigation, sources in the investigating agency said.
The controversy surrounding procurement of books for Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore | Explained
Periyar Arivulagam books row: People of Tamil Nadu will never forgive DMK for corruption, says CM Vijay
Library book ‘scam’: Madras High Court had sounded warning two years ago, called for enquiry

The issue was flagged by noted Tamil writer Perumal Murugan who visited the library in Coimbatore recently and pointed to issues relating to price, quality and authenticity of content in some books. The agency is looking into allegations of names of fictitious authors, fabrication of International Standard Book Number (ISBNs), depiction of factual errors and higher book prices.
During the search at Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore on Tuesday, DVAC sleuths scrutinised documents pertaining to book purchase in the administrative section of the library, on the third floor.
The DVAC would register a case if prima facie evidence is established in the detailed inquiry.

articles.title: Moody’s ups India’s FY27 growth estimate to 7% on broad-based momentum
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7% over the medium term, Moody's said

Moody's Ratings on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) said the Indian economy is expected to grow at a higher rate of 7 per cent in the current fiscal, led by broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience.

In its Global Macro Outlook 2027-28, Moody's, however, said that near-term risks to growth persist as household consumption remains vulnerable to “intensifying and broadening price pressures”, with headline inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 2-6% target range, while a deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions will weigh on agricultural output and rural demand.
“India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7% from 6.5%,” it said.
Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7% over the medium term, Moody's said.
A sustained private investment boom that materially boosts manufacturing, employment and productivity could lift growth rates above Moody's baseline projections.

articles.title: Alice Huang, who reportedly had affair with Nvidia CEO, is Chinese banker turned tech exec
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: An affair between Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who reportedly was suspected of working as a spy for Beijing, has rocked the tech and political worlds

She was building a career in Chinese finance before turning to tech with a leadership role at a data centre company in Singapore. He is the high-profile CEO of Nvidia, the California-based company that makes computer chips relied upon by advanced artificial intelligence systems.
An affair between Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who reportedly was suspected of working as a spy for Beijing, has rocked the tech and political worlds.
The Chinese businesswoman also known as Huang Le had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, according to reports over the past month by the New York Times.

The newspaper also reported that top policymakers were informed in a memo that intelligence indicated she was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, recruited to influence Nvidia to make its most advanced chips more available in China.

In one widely shared photograph of the pair, Jensen Huang and people surrounding him are holding drinks in Taipei, while Alice Huang sits behind him, apparently watching him in conversation. The picture was posted in 2024 by software company NetThunder to its LinkedIn page.
It remains unclear how long the affair lasted, and when exactly the relationship might have ended. The Associated Press was unable to reach Alice Huang for comment.
Publicly available information about Alice Huang is scant.
She was a Chinese finance executive before becoming involved in artificial intelligence, data centres and computer chips.

In 2023, she became a director at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which describes itself as an “NVIDIA cloud partner”. Last year, Megaspeed faced scrutiny from the U.S. over its alleged skirting of U.S. export restrictions and routing of a large amount of advanced Nvidia chips for Chinese users.

Megaspeed was incorporated in 2015 in Singapore with the name 7Road International, after being spun off as the overseas arm of a Chinese video game developer, according to corporate registration records.

articles.title: Iran says tanker struck mine, caught fire in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait

Iran's army said on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) that an oil tanker had struck a mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, where the country has been targeting ships that transit without its authorisation.
Since the outbreak of the West Asia war in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.
The United States has, in response, imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.
The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait.

"Early this morning, a violating oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in an unsafe, prohibited area in the east of the Strait of Hormuz," the naval forces of Iran's army said in a statement carried by state TV.
In recent weeks Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships had caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.

U.S. Central Command, which oversees U.S. military operations in the region, has been escorting ships through the waterway and said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
On Tuesday (November 10), the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said three other oil tankers had caught fire in the strait.

articles.title: Firecrackers still Delhi’s top pollutant after Deepavali, IITM finds
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The contribution of firecrackers to the city's pollution levels was significantly higher on November 9, a day after Deepavali, before declining on November 11, the IITM models showed

Firecrackers emerged as the biggest contributor to Delhi's air pollution on both Monday (November 9, 2026) and Tuesday (November 10), accounting for 71.1% and 29.8% of the pollution load, respectively, according to source-apportionment estimates by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM).

The contribution of firecrackers to the city's pollution levels was significantly higher on Monday (November 9), a day after Deepavali, before declining on Tuesday (November 11), the IITM models showed.

The estimates had a standard deviation (SD) of 104.1 percentage points on Monday (November 9) and 27.7 percentage points on Tuesday (November 10), indicating considerable variability and uncertainty in the modelled contributions.

On Monday (November 9), vehicular emissions accounted for 6.9% of the pollution, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols at 5% and secondary organic aerosols at 4.5%. Mixed or unresolved biofuel contributed 4.45%, while mineral dust and ash and mixed combustion accounted for 2.5% each.

Wood burning contributed 1.3%, while waste burning, including municipal and plastic-rubber-containing waste, accounted for 1.1%. Coal combustion and industrial emissions contributed 0.5% and 0.2%, respectively.
On Tuesday (November 10), the contribution of firecrackers dropped to 29.8%, while secondary organic aerosols emerged as the second-largest contributor at 17.5%.
Vehicular emissions and secondary inorganic aerosols each accounted for 11.7% of the pollution load, while wood burning contributed 10.7% and waste burning 7.7%.
Vehicular emissions emerged as the third largest contributor to pollution on Tuesday (November 10).
Mixed combustion accounted for 5.1%, followed by mixed or unresolved biofuel at 3.3% and mineral dust and ash at 1.5%.
Delhi's average 24-hour Air Quality Index (AQI) had improved marginally to the 'poor' category on Tuesday (November 10), with the 4 p.m. reading settling at 299.

Wood burning contributed 1.3%, while waste burning, including municipal and plastic-rubber-containing waste, accounted for 1.1%. Coal combustion and industrial emissions contributed 0.5% and 0.2%, respectively.

On Tuesday (November 10), the contribution of firecrackers dropped to 29.8%, while secondary organic aerosols emerged as the second-largest contributor at 17.5%.

Vehicular emissions and secondary inorganic aerosols each accounted for 11.7% of the pollution load, while wood burning contributed 10.7% and waste burning 7.7%.

Vehicular emissions emerged as the third largest contributor to pollution on Tuesday (November 10).

Mixed combustion accounted for 5.1%, followed by mixed or unresolved biofuel at 3.3% and mineral dust and ash at 1.5%.

Delhi's average 24-hour Air Quality Index (AQI) had improved marginally to the 'poor' category on Tuesday (November 10), with the 4 p.m. reading settling at 299.

articles.title: WhatsApp to simplify communication on app, add financial services
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Meta’s head of WhatsApp Kunal Shah shared a post outlining some largely expected outcomes for the messaging platform
Meta’s new head of WhatsApp, Kunal Shah, has promised simplified calls/messages and more financial services on the messaging platform, apart from increased AI integration.
In a post on the social media platform X on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), Mr. Shah said he had spent around four months at WhatsApp.
He also shared some largely expected goals for the platform.
The WhatsApp executive said he would make voice notes, groups, stickers and video “simpler and more expressive.”

The company is also working with financial services and telecom partners to explore processes such as paying bills, borrowing money, and ensuring connectivity during travel. The aim of this step is to keep users within the messaging platform, even if they are completing other personal finance tasks.
Not surprisingly, Mr. Shah said he wanted to make these features more efficient with AI.
He did not announce any specific features or share a release date for the same.
WhatsApp handles over 100 billion messages and 2 billion calls every day, he shared, while stressing that the company’s principles would not change any time soon.

“Your personal messages and calls stay end-to-end encrypted. This and our quality bar stays the same. What happens inside WhatsApp only matters for what it makes possible outside it: more time together, stronger communities, and fewer barriers between people and the lives they want to live,” shared Mr. Shah.

articles.title: Faith meets fitness: The Keralam church where prayers come with pull-ups
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, has set up an open gym to promote fitness among parishioners. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

articles.title: Kedarnath temple portals closed for winter; deity's palanquin begins journey to Ukhimath
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The process began at 4 a.m. with special prayers and religious ceremonies, with all rituals performed in accordance with traditional customs before the temple doors were closed at the auspicious time
The portals of the Kedarnath shrine were closed for the winter season at 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) following prescribed rituals and the chanting of Vedic mantras.

The process began at 4 a.m. with special prayers and religious ceremonies, with all rituals performed in accordance with traditional customs before the temple doors were closed at the auspicious time.
Following the closure, the processional palanquin of Lord Kedarnath was carried around the temple complex before departing for the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath, the deity's winter abode.

According to the schedule, the palanquin will halt overnight at Rampur on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) before reaching Guptkashi on November 12. It will arrive at the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath on November 13.
For the next six months, devotees can offer prayers to the deity at the Omkareshwar Temple.
The ceremonial palanquin of Goddess Yamuna, led by Shani Dev Maharaj, departed from Yamunotri for Kharsali, the deity’s winter abode, amid traditional rituals and folk music.
Villagers and pilgrims accorded a grand welcome to the palanquin upon its arrival in the afternoon at the ancestral village of the goddess, showering it with flowers and garlands.
During the six-month pilgrimage season, the Yamunotri Temple Committee received more than ₹90 lakh in donations through donation boxes and receipt books.

On Tuesday (November 10, 2026), a day before the closure of the temple, the committee opened the donation boxes for the fourth time to count the offerings. The exercise yielded ₹10 lakh 42 thousand in cash, while approximately ₹6 lakh was collected through receipt books.

articles.title: Jagan alleges large-scale malpractice in Andhra local body polls; says YSRCP vote share rose
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: YSRCP leaders allege bouncers at counting centres, rejected votes and recounts that changed results

YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has accused the Telugu Desam Party (TDP-led) government of resorting to large-scale electoral malpractice in the recent local body elections to conceal the growing public support for his party.

At a meeting with party leaders from several districts at Tadepalli on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), Mr. Jagan reviewed the conduct of the elections and alleged that irregularities, intimidation and manipulation had taken place at various stages of the electoral process, from the announcement of the schedule to the counting of votes.

మున్సిపల్, ఎంపీటీసీ, జెడ్పీటీసీ ఎన్నికలు జరిగిన తీరుపై పార్టీ కేంద్ర కార్యాలయంలో వివిధ జిల్లా నాయకులతో కలిసి సమీక్షించిన వైయస్ జగన్ గారు టీడీపీ దౌర్జన్యాలు, దాడులకి ఎదురు నిలిచి నాయకులతో పాటు కార్యకర్తలు గట్టిగా పోరాటం చేశారని వైయస్ జగన్ గారు కితాబు ఎన్నికలు సజావుగా జరిగి ఉంటే వైయస్‌‌ఆర్‌సీపీ ఓటింగ్ శాతం ఇంకా పెరిగేదన్న వైయస్ జగన్ గారు.. చంద్రబాబు ప్రభుత్వం తప్పుల్ని కప్పిపుచ్చుకోవడానికి అక్రమాలకి పాల్పడిందని మండిపాటు తమ రాజకీయ జీవితంలో ఈ తరహాలో ఎన్నికల్లో అక్రమాలను చూడలేదని వైయస్ జగన్ గారికి చెప్పిన పార్టీ సీనియర్ నేతలు

The YSRCP’s vote share had increased compared with the 2024 elections despite the alleged irregularities, he said. The party would have secured a much higher vote share had the elections been conducted in a free and fair manner, he added.

Accusing Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu of misusing official machinery, Mr. Jagan said the ruling party had resorted to undemocratic practices because of the growing support for the YSRCP and the declining popularity of the government. New methods of electoral manipulation had been adopted, including attempts to reverse results in places where YSRCP candidates had won, he alleged.
He also accused Mr. Naidu of trying to divert attention from the alleged irregularities by raising questions about the local body elections held during the previous YSRCP regime.

Party leaders who attended the meeting reportedly described the recent elections as unprecedented in terms of irregularities and alleged that the State Election Commission had failed to ensure a free and fair electoral process.
They alleged that bouncers were deployed at counting centres in place of authorised election agents and that relatives of candidates were kidnapped to force them to withdraw their nominations.

The leaders further alleged that large numbers of votes polled in favour of YSRCP candidates were declared invalid during counting and that power supply was deliberately disrupted at some counting centres to facilitate manipulation.

They also complained that repeated recounting was ordered in constituencies where YSRCP candidates had secured victories, allegedly resulting in changes to the final tallies. However, requests for recounting made by YSRCP candidates were rejected, they said.

articles.title: Two days past Deepavali, NPCI yet to announce a date for UPI MDR rollout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: About a month ago, when the NPCI had pushed back the rollout of MDR from its original date of October 15, it had said it would be implemented “immediately post Diwali”

articles.title: Russia, Ukraine hold second day of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: ‘We are starting the second day of negotiations,’ Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service, who leads Kyiv's delegation in Abu Dhabi, says on social media

Delegations from Moscow and Kyiv on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) held a second straight day of U.S.-brokered talks on ways of ending the war started by Russia's all-out invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.

Hopes are low for any breakthrough in the first meeting in nine months between the delegations, although U.S. officials say they are determined to revive peace efforts that so far have failed to deliver significant results.
“We are starting the second day of negotiations,” Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service who leads Kyiv's delegation in Abu Dhabi, said on social media.

The envoys met for four hours on Tuesday (November 10) in the capital of the United Arab Emirates, which was chosen as a neutral venue. The talks, mediated by U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and envoy Steve Witkoff, were due to conclude later Wednesday (November 11).

The context of the negotiations has changed since the last meeting in February in Geneva. The Trump administration has to reckon with Democrats, who could demand more support for Ukraine, taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections.
Also, Russia's wartime economy is under heavy strain, and Ukraine is reeling from devastating aerial attacks on its power grid.
Mr. Umerov said that Wednesday (November 11) would begin with three-way talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States, with Kyiv's delegation meeting afterwards with European officials.
Moscow doesn't want European countries, which are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent, involved in the direct negotiations.
However, representatives of European governments, the European Union and NATO were in Abu Dhabi and were consulting with the Ukrainian delegation, officials said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday's (November 10) session was “constructive and quite substantive”.

articles.title: Pakistan Deputy PM Ishaq Dar's grandson, seven others indicted in Lahore gang rape case
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: All the suspects, presently in judicial custody, were produced before the trial court for the indictment proceedings

A Pakistani court has indicted eight suspects, including the grandson of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, in a gang rape of two foreign women, an official said on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

"Lahore's Additional District & Sessions Judge (AD&SJ) Rafaqat Ali Gondal on Tuesday (November 10) framed charges against the suspects who pleaded not guilty," a court official said and added the judge directed the prosecution to present its witnesses on December 9 so that the formal trial proceedings could be commenced.
All the suspects, presently in judicial custody, were produced before the trial court for the indictment proceedings.
Ironically, Punjab police had already given a "clean chit" to Ishaq Dar's grandson Raza Dar and his four accomplices in this case.

Police not only absolved Dar's grandson and his four friends of rape charges but charged three other low-paid employees of him of raping the women, as per a police report earlier submitted in the court.

The two women, one from the Netherlands and the other from Venezuela, were allegedly kidnapped and raped by Raza Dar and four of his friends after arriving in Lahore on a business trip in June this year.
The medical examination confirmed that the foreign women were raped. Both victim women after recording their statements had left for their home countries.
According to the police report, the victim women said that they met Raza Dar in Singapore in 2025 and invited him to invest money with them in the business of crypto currency.
After getting profit returns on initial investment, Raza Dar invested over $500,000.

"However, this time, the women did not give any profit or return the amount to the suspect," the report said, adding in June this year, the suspect invited both women to Pakistan on the pretext of a meeting with another investor, where they stayed at a hotel in Islamabad and travelled to Murree hill station with their free will.

articles.title: Anaemia prevention in India: pivoting towards better multidimensional strategies
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: If anaemia reduction should align with India’s goals for NCD reduction, then the focus must be on better diets through diversification. That should be non-negotiable for public health policy: no amount of papering over cracks with pills and potions will work in the long term

India has had decades of unchanged high anaemia prevalence in women and children that has historically been thought to be due to iron deficiency. This has led firstly to an iron and folic acid (IFA) tablet supplementation targeted at women and children, and secondly to fitful implementation of mandatory fortification of staple foods. IFA is a ‘precision’ strategy, applying as it does to the vulnerable population it is intended for, while fortification is a broad strategy that applies to the entire population. The latter works in controlled settings such as clinical trials, but has not worked in real-world settings, and might have adverse effects when given to those it is unintended for.

The reason for pivoting: anaemia is mistakenly conflated with iron deficiency In India. The evidence is otherwise: in national Indian surveys, it has been shown that iron deficiency is not the major cause of anaemia. Indeed, fully one-third of anaemia cases demonstrate no micronutrient deficiency or obvious cause. Even so, giving iron should have sorted out those who did have iron deficiency anaemia, and reduced the general anaemia prevalence. While this could be a problem with inefficient programme implementation, two important questions arise: is there is really a deficiency in dietary iron intake in India? And is the administered iron being adequately absorbed and utilised for haemoglobin formation?

Science, Space & Environment Report: Anaemia prevention in India: pivoting towards better multidimensional strategies. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Khaki whistle guards to replace metal chains for Karnataka police
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police constables and head constables in Karnataka will soon replace the traditional metal whistle chains on their uniforms with new khaki-coloured whistle guards, following an order issued by Director-General and Inspector-General of Police (DG&IGP) M.A. Saleem.

Mr. Saleem, who is also the Head of the Police Force (HoPF), has directed all unit officers to take necessary steps to introduce the new whistle guards for lower-rank police personnel across the State.

The move follows concerns that metal whistle chains fitted to police uniforms tend to rust due to weather conditions. The rust stains uniforms, leaving permanent marks and damaging the fabric. Prolonged contact with rusted metal may also cause skin problems and other health-related issues, according to a representation submitted to the authorities.

Several other States have already replaced metal whistle chains with whistle guards, using khaki- or blue-coloured alternatives. The proposal for Karnataka police personnel was to introduce whistle guards in a colour matching the navy-blue peaked caps issued as part of the uniform, or in another colour selected by the department.

Mohan Kumar Danappa, a member of the Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority, had repeatedly written to the Home Department and the DGP, urging the introduction of whistle guards and matte-finish buttons for police personnel. He had also submitted photographs of police uniforms in other States where these changes had been implemented.
The proposal was announced by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar during the Police Martyrs’ Day programme in October.

articles.title: TDB under fire as Sabarimala pilgrimage readiness faces delays
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The union said that although the Chief Minister directed tar and make roads to the parking areas motorable during his Nilakkal visit, many stretches remain muddy and essential repairs are delayed.

The delay in key preparatory works ahead of the annual Sabarimala pilgrimage season has drawn sharp criticism from Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) employees, who have held the leadership responsible for the lapses.

the Travancore Devaswom Employees Front, a Congress-backed employees’ union, has now come up flagging delays in completing essential infrastructure works and warned that inadequate preparations could disrupt the pilgrimage season.

“The Chief Minister had directed that the roads leading to the parking grounds be tarred and made motorable during his visit to Nilakkal. However, several stretches remain muddy even now. Essential repair works have also not been completed on time. The new construction work at the aravana plant, which was scheduled for completion during the previous monthly pooja, remains unfinished,” the union said in a statement.

More worrying is the dwindling stock of ghee required for aravana production, even as the tender process for procuring additional supplies from outside remains incomplete. Any delay in securing ghee could seriously affect production and distribution of the offering during the pilgrimage season, the union warned.

It held the Board president and administrative committee responsible for any disruption in aravana production, ghee supply, appam availability, transport facilities, sanitation or food arrangements for employees. The union also warned against attempts to shift the blame for administrative failures onto employees.”Employees working sincerely despite limited facilities should not be made scapegoats for the Board’s failure to make adequate preparations,” it said.
Besides the employees’ union, several other organisations, including the Akhil Bharata Ayyappa Seva Sanghom, have also expressed dissatisfaction over the pace of preparatory works at Sabarimala.

The board, meanwhile, acknowledged that some works had fallen behind schedule but maintained that they could be completed before the season begins. Its officials also alleged that the Congress-backed union was attempting to pre-empt criticism of its own leadership in the event of any lapses during the pilgrimage season.

The delay in upgrading the aravana plant was one of the major setbacks, a Board official admitted. ”One of the major lapses was on the part of the Devaswom PWD, which delayed the upgradation of the aravana plant by around 15 days. However, the situation is under control, as production of three lakh tins of aravana began on Monday,” the official said.

Even as the board sought to allay concerns over production, the distribution of the offering remains another potential trouble spot. Officials fear that poor internet connectivity at Sannidhanam and possible software glitches could disrupt transactions at the counters. ”As many as 19 counters will operate at Sannidhanam to distribute the offerings, all equipped with an integrated payment system. However, there are serious doubts about whether this arrangement can be sustained smoothly in the long run,” the official added.

articles.title: Cabinet approves ₹2,390 crore metro rail link from Noida Sector 51 to Greater Noida Sector 4
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The project, approved by the Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, represents a significant advancement in the city's infrastructure development, an official statement said

The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) approved the extension of the Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor from Noida Sector 51 to Greater Noida Sector 4 at an estimated cost of ₹2,390 crore, with a length of 8.449 kilometres and five elevated stations.
The project, approved by the Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, represents a significant advancement in the city's infrastructure development, an official statement said.
The Prime Minister listed the advantages of the project, saying it would provide a major boost to connectivity and ease of living.

"As Noida and Greater Noida grow, why should daily commutes become longer? Here is some good news for the people of Noida and Greater Noida! The Cabinet has approved an extension of the Aqua Line Metro.”
"Key advantages — easier access to offices, schools, hospitals and commercial hubs. Less congestion.”
“Shorter commutes. A major boost to connectivity and ease of living indeed," Mr. Modi said in a post on X.
The project would be completed over a period of four years, Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw told reporters at a Cabinet briefing.
Upon operationalisation of this corridor, Noida and Greater Noida will have 71.878 kilometres of active metro rail network, he said.
Mr. Vaishnaw said this project acts as a major expansion of the metro rail network in the city.
The corridor will introduce approximately 8.449 kilometres of new metro lines, significantly improving public transportation in Noida and Greater Noida, which currently lack efficient connectivity.

fullParagraphs: Traffic movement on six key roads in Mysuru, including stretches leading to Chamundi Hill, will be regulated on November 12 and 13 in view of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the city on Friday.
Mr. Modi is scheduled to inaugurate an LED dome planetarium during his visit.

The roads where traffic diversions will be in force include Lalitadripura Road (from Lalitadripura Ring Road junction to Helipad junction); IVAC Road (from IVAC junction to Chamundi Hill Road junction); Lalith Mahal Road (from T. Narasipur Road T junction to M.R.C. Circle); Chamundi Hill Road (from Sangolli Rayanna Circle to Chamundi Hill); Lorry Terminal Road (from M.R.C. Circle to Rajahamsa junction); and Nanjangud Road (from Rajahamsa junction to Nanjangud Ring Road junction).

The police have suggested an alternative route for vehicles proceeding towards Chamundi Hill from Sangolli Rayanna Circle. Motorists can take the route via Gautama Buddha Circle, M.M. Road, R. Junction, Savitri Bai Phule Circle, Ring Road and Uttanahalli Ring Road before joining Chamundi Hill Road, a press release from the Commissioner of Police said.
The police have advised motorists to avoid the above mentioned road stretches and take alternative routes during the two days.
The police have urged motorists to plan their journeys in advance, use alternative routes wherever possible and follow the instructions of traffic personnel.

articles.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to major prisoner swap after U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The two sides have exchanged thousands of captured soldiers throughout the almost five-year war, started by Russia’s 2022 invasion
Russia and Ukraine have agreed their biggest ever release of prisoners after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner told reporters on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).
“One of the positives is that we agreed that we’re going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners, and we’re going to finalise the numbers tomorrow,” he said.

Mr. Kushner and fellow U.S. mediator Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday (November 12, 2026) to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
The two sides have exchanged thousands of captured soldiers throughout the almost five-year war, started by Russia’s 2022 invasion.
But diplomatic talks have so far failed to move the two sides closer to an agreement to halt the fighting, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people.

The two days of conversations in Abu Dhabi appeared to fit that mould, with the prisoner exchange and agreement to carry on talking the only concrete outcomes mentioned by any side in post-talks press statements.
Russian envoy Vladimir Medinsky and Ukrainian negotiator Rustem Umerov also said a large scale prisoner exchange had been agreed, adding the numbers would be announced later.

Delegations from Moscow and Kyiv on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) held a second straight day of U.S.-brokered talks on ways of ending the war started by Russia's all-out invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.

The envoys met for four hours on Tuesday (November 10) in the capital of the United Arab Emirates, which was chosen as a neutral venue. The talks, mediated by U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and envoy Steve Witkoff, were due to conclude later Wednesday (November 11).

The context of the negotiations has changed since the last meeting in February in Geneva. The Trump administration has to reckon with Democrats, who could demand more support for Ukraine, taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections.

articles.title: 51-year-old woman undergoes mechanical mitral valve replacement at Gandhi Hospital
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Doctors at the Gandhi Hospital, Secunderabad, successfully conducted a mitral valve replacement (MVR) surgery on a 51-year-old woman recently.

The patient, Rajamma, was admitted to the Department of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery (CTVS) with complaints of breathlessness, classified as New York Heart Association Class III, indicating marked limitation of physical activity due to cardiac symptoms.

Following routine investigations, doctors performed an MVR procedure using a 27-mm mechanical valve. Post-surgery, she was shifted to the ICU and placed on mechanical ventilation with minimal inotropic support. She was successfully taken off ventilator support on the first post-operative day.

Anticoagulation therapy was subsequently initiated to prevent blood clot formation around the artificial valve. A postoperative 2D echocardiography with colour Doppler showed normally functioning mechanical valve leaflets, minimal pressure gradient across the prosthetic valve, no paravalvular leak and good left ventricular function. The patient has been declared fit for discharge, doctors said.

articles.title: Yadgir farmers who received less than the announced compensation demand full amount
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Most farmers have received only ₹1,200, ₹1,500 or ₹2,000 in their accounts instead of the declared compensation amount in the first installment’

​Farmers in distress in Yadgir district have urged the State government to rectify errors in the disbursement of drought compensation within a week saying that a majority of beneficiaries have received significantly lower amounts than what has been officially announced.

​Addressing a press conference here on Wednesday, social activist Umesh Mudnal said that Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, during a video interaction recently, announced financial relief of ₹2,500 per acre for affected farmers via direct benefit transfer (DBT), with a promised second installment of ₹2,500 to follow within 15 days.
However, most farmers have received only ₹1,200, ₹1,500 or ₹2,000 in their accounts instead of the declared amount in the first installment, Mr. Mudnal said.

He demanded that the State government immediately correct the discrepancies and credit the full compensation amount within seven days, warning of a widespread agitation if the issue remains unaddressed.
​Mr. Mudnal also targeted local officials, saying that the Revenue and Agriculture departments have failed to conduct proper field surveys to assess the actual extent of drought damage.

“Farmers in Yadgir have been continuously affected by extreme weather, suffering under severe droughts and floods year after year. The district administration must ensure that proper crop loss assessments are conducted in strict accordance with regulations so that affected farmers receive fair compensation,” he said.

​Echoing the grievance, a farmer from Saidapur village Srishail, who attended the press conference, shared that he received only ₹1,500 instead of the announced ₹2,500. He said that prolonged dry spells and severe drought have completely wiped out the cotton crop he cultivated in his 10-acre dryland.
​Farmers Mahesh, Yallesh, Hanumanth and Shivakumar were among those present at the press conference.

articles.title: Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Goa Vande Bharat Express users may pay nearly ₹200 more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Charging fares inflating the distance by 40% on Konkan Railway network between Thokur and Madgaon and 100% on 55 km Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya Road Ghat section the reason for extra fares

From November 15, patrons of the Yeshwantpur-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express (Train No. 26655/656) will pay nearly ₹200 extra fare in chair car (CC) and about ₹300 extra on executive chair car (EC) when compared to the same distance travelled on other Vande Bharat services.

The actual base fare, for example, between Yeshwantpur and Madgaon in CC would be around ₹1,186 and in EC around ₹2,444. However, the actual distance of 670 km gets inflated to around 844 km increasing the base fare to ₹1,369 in CC (₹183 extra) and ₹2,795 (₹351 extra) in EC classes. The base fare excludes reservation charges of ₹40 and ₹60, superfast charges of ₹45 and ₹75, respectively, for these classes and 5% GST on all these charges. If the passenger opts for onboard food, catering charges ranging from ₹300 to ₹600, would be extra.

For Karwar, the likely base fare could be ₹1,292 as against the actual ₹1,100 in CC (₹192 extra) and ₹2,642 as against ₹2,253 in EC class; for Udupi, it could be ₹931 as against ₹809 (₹122 extra) in CC and ₹1,890 as against ₹1,651 (₹239 extra) in EC and for Mangaluru Junction, the base fare could be ₹809 as against the actual ₹721 (₹88 extra) in CC and ₹1,561 as against the actual ₹1,468 (₹93 extra) in EC class.
Source: Railway Ministry’s fare chart for premium services

Normal fares are collected on other VB expresses operating in Karnataka for almost similar distances. For example, the base fares on Mangaluru-Thiruvananthapuram Central VB Express have been ₹1,131 and ₹2,295 for CC and EC respectively for 620 km distance; KSR Bengaluru-Ernakulam Junction VB Express at ₹1,159 and ₹2,352 for 625 km; KSR Bengaluru-Belagavi VB Express at ₹1,132 and ₹2,295 for 612 km and on Yeshwantpur-Kacheguda VB, the base fares have been ₹1,113 and ₹2,267 for CC and EC respectively.
A 16-car Brand new Vande Bharat rake is kept ready for the November 15 inaugural run of Madgaon-Yeshwantpur VB Express from Mangaluru Junction on November 11, 2026. | Photo Credit: H S MANJUNATH

The extra fare becomes applicable as the Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd., (KRCL) on whose network half of the route passes through, inflates the distance by 40% to calculate passenger fares and by 50% for freight charges. KRCL network begins from Thokur near Mangaluru and extends till Roha in Maharashtra surpassing Madgaon. Thus, about 300 km distance between Thokur and Madgaon gets inflated to 416 km.

At the same time, the South Western Railway (SWR) inflates the 55 km distance on the Ghat section between Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road by 100%, making the chargeable distance to 110 km. Thus, the end-to-end inflated chargeable distance becomes about 844 km against the actual 670 km distance.

The SWR justified the inflated distance saying the Indian Railways follows the practice on almost all Ghat routes because of the challenges in operating through difficult terrains. KRCL was initially allowed to inflate the distance to recover the construction cost of about ₹3,555 crore. The Corporation now justifies the additional collection due to “heavy maintenance cost (due to difficult geographical conditions).”

articles.title: Brazil electoral court fines Meta, sees no deliberate election bias
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Meta told the Court last month it had adopted ​measures to ensure equal treatment of ‌the two campaigns

Brazil's electoral authority fined Meta's Facebook 7.5 million reais ($1.34 million) for failing to fully comply ​with judicial orders during last month's Presidential election runoff campaign, but said there ‌was no evidence so far that the company had ​deliberately acted to influence the outcome.

In a unanimous decision, ⁠the country's top electoral court (TSE) ruled on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that Facebook had failed to adequately meet court demands related to allegations that its ‌platform treated content from the rival campaigns of leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator ‌Flavio Bolsonaro differently.

Mr. Lula's coalition filed a complaint ahead of the ‌vote alleging ⁠restrictions on the distribution of its posts, the activity ⁠of purportedly inauthentic accounts, failures in identifying AI-generated content, and asymmetries in the operation of Meta's tools.
Meta told the Court last month it had adopted ​measures to ensure equal treatment of ‌the two campaigns. It did not immediately reply to a fresh request for comment.

The Court said Meta had provided some information and documents on the measures, but found that ‌parts of its orders were either not complied with, were ​only partially fulfilled, or were carried out after deadlines had passed.

"The records contain technical failures acknowledged ⁠by Facebook itself, but there are no elements allowing us to conclude, on a preliminary basis, that there was deliberate action to unbalance ‌the election," Justice Marco Aurelio Bellizze wrote in his ruling.
"That conclusion would require robust evidence, to be produced through the appropriate legal proceedings," he added.

According to Mr. Bellizze, the fine reflected Meta's conduct in responding to the Court orders as a whole, including delays, incomplete information and difficulties in verifying some of ‌the data submitted.

The amount corresponds to three daily fines of 500,000 reais between October ​17 and 19, and six days of fines of 1 million reais per day between October 20 ⁠and 25, when Mr. Lula unexpectedly secured re-election over Mr. Bolsonaro after his ⁠team mobilised a huge social media campaign.

Mr. Lula has long vowed to tighten rules on social media in the country. ‌In his victory speech, he said, "We had to overcome foreign interference in the election, coming from outside through digital platforms ​that we will have to regulate."

articles.title: New registration framework proposed to strengthen allied and healthcare professions in India
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions invites public and stakeholder comments on the Draft Provisional Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), under the Union Ministry of Health, has proposed a comprehensive regulatory framework for the registration of allied and healthcare professionals, with pathways for skill upgradation, competency assessment, and transition to regular registration.

The broad categories of allied and healthcare professions governed by the NCAHP include clinical laboratories, surgical and emergency technology, physiotherapy, nutrition, ophthalmology, occupational therapy, community and behavioural health, medical imaging, physician associates, and health informatics.

The proposed framework aims for uniformity, transparency and accountability in professional registration. Practitioners can enhance their competencies in keeping with prescribed standards, a release issued by the Ministry said.
Key features of the proposed regulations include the establishment of a standardised mechanism for provisional registration in accordance with the NCAHP Act, 2021.

“Importantly, the proposed Regulations also provide opportunities for eligible provisionally registered professionals to undertake prescribed bridge courses for skill enhancement, supervised clinical training and minimum qualifying examinations, wherever applicable, to meet the requirements for regular registration,’’ the Healthy Ministry’s statement said.
This competency-based approach seeks to facilitate professional development and career progression, and improve the quality of allied and healthcare services.
“The proposed framework places emphasis on skill development, professional competence and regulatory accountability,’’ a senior Health Ministry official said.

By linking progression to regular registration with prescribed requirements, the regulations seek to ensure allied and healthcare professionals possess the necessary knowledge and clinical competencies to deliver quality healthcare services.
An integrated online registration system for submitting applications, verifying credentials, assess eligibility, and issue provisional registration certificates is also proposed.

Eligible professionals granted provisional registration will receive a Provisional Registration Unique Identification Number (PR UID). The digital platform will simply procedures, improve access, and promote uniform efficiency across States and Union Territories.

articles.title: JSP Salur chairperson accuses Minister of supporting independent candidate
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A war of words erupted between Jana Sena Party’s newly elected Chairperson of Salur Gorle Vijaya Kumari and the supporters of Minister for Tribal Welfare Gummadi Sandhya Rani after former accused the Minister of supporting independent candidate Gulla Manjeera and violating the alliance guidelines during the recently concluded local body polls.

Despite JSP being part of the alliance parties, Ms. Kumari alleged that the Minister Rani had backed Ms. Manjeera, who got 6,143 votes, resulting in the loss of JSP Councillors in three wards of the seven wards they contested in. She also claimed that all the independent candidates were allotted same symbol – “cupboard”, causing a lot of confusion in voters.
In the Municipal elections in Salur conducted on November 1, Mr. Kumari polled 9,686 votes, while her nearest rival and YSRCP candidate Ribka Rani got 9,390 votes.
JSP Salur Coordinator Gorle Tirupati Naidu asserted that the violation of “alliance dharma” would be brought to the notice of JSP high command in a couple of days.
Questioning the logic behind allocation of ‘cupboard’ symbol to all independent candidates, Mr. Naidu alleged that “it [independent candidates] was an unofficial panel created to defeat JSP”.
Meanwhile, supporters of the Minister refuted the allegations and said that JSP candidates were defeated in the absence of a dedicated network at ground level.
Meanwhile, for the deputy chairperson’s post YSRCP won 13 wards, while TDP got 11 seats in Salur elections.

JSP won four and independents got elected in three places. A BJP candidate was elected in one ward. Former Deputy Chief Minister and YSRCP senior leader Peedika Rajanna Dora hoped that their party would win the deputy chairperson’s post as it is the single largest party in the council.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

A war of words erupted between Jana Sena Party’s newly elected Chairperson of Salur Gorle Vijaya Kumari and the supporters of Minister for Tribal Welfare Gummadi Sandhya Rani after former accused the Minister of supporting independent candidate Gulla Manjeera and violating the alliance guidelines during the recently concluded local body polls.

Despite JSP being part of the alliance parties, Ms. Kumari alleged that the Minister Rani had backed Ms. Manjeera, who got 6,143 votes, resulting in the loss of JSP Councillors in three wards of the seven wards they contested in. She also claimed that all the independent candidates were allotted same symbol – “cupboard”, causing a lot of confusion in voters.

In the Municipal elections in Salur conducted on November 1, Mr. Kumari polled 9,686 votes, while her nearest rival and YSRCP candidate Ribka Rani got 9,390 votes.

JSP Salur Coordinator Gorle Tirupati Naidu asserted that the violation of “alliance dharma” would be brought to the notice of JSP high command in a couple of days.

Questioning the logic behind allocation of ‘cupboard’ symbol to all independent candidates, Mr. Naidu alleged that “it [independent candidates] was an unofficial panel created to defeat JSP”.

Meanwhile, supporters of the Minister refuted the allegations and said that JSP candidates were defeated in the absence of a dedicated network at ground level.

Meanwhile, for the deputy chairperson’s post YSRCP won 13 wards, while TDP got 11 seats in Salur elections.

JSP won four and independents got elected in three places. A BJP candidate was elected in one ward. Former Deputy Chief Minister and YSRCP senior leader Peedika Rajanna Dora hoped that their party would win the deputy chairperson’s post as it is the single largest party in the council.

articles.title: Farmer climbs tree on Shivamogga DC office premises, alleges corruption against Revenue Dept. officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tension prevailed for some time on the premises of the Deputy Commissioner’s office here on Wednesday after a farmer climbed a tree and threatened to jump off, alleging corruption by Revenue Department officials.

N. Nagaraj, 55, from Ramenakoppa village in Shivamogga taluk, climbed a huge banyan tree on the premises and refused to come down even after his relatives and officials appealed to him. Personnel of the Fire and Emergency Services were summoned.

Mr. Nagaraj said the then Deputy Commissioner had passed an order in August, in a land ownership dispute, in favour of him and a few other litigants. The tahsildar, who was to act on the order after verifying the relevant records, delayed the process and took money from the litigants, he alleged. He said he and the other litigants were worried because the tahsildar had been transferred the previous day.

After repeated persuasion by officials and relatives, Mr. Nagaraj agreed to come down. Fire and Emergency Services personnel helped him down with a ladder. He then told the media that a few Revenue Department officials took money to implement the Deputy Commissioner’s order and even demanded more. Later, he met Deputy Commissioner Prakash G.T. Nittali and submitted a petition.

When The Hindu c ontacted the Deputy Commissioner, Mr. Nittali said he had gathered information from the farmer about the issue. “The previous Deputy Commissioner issued an order, and the tahsildar has to act as per the order. The new tahsildar took charge of the office this morning. He will take up the issue and act as per law. I have told him the same,” he said.
On the allegations of corruption, he said that if there were specific allegations against anyone, backed by concrete evidence, he could order an inquiry and take further action.

articles.title: Mudhol farmers demand ₹5,500 for a tonne of sugarcane
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: District Minister appeals to them to call off their strike
The protest by sugarcane farmers in Mudhol in Bagalkot district demanding ₹5,500 per tonne, entered the sixth day on Wednesday.
Activists took out a rally from Sangolli Rayanna Circle to the taluk office and submitted a memorandum to the State government.
They vowed to continue their protest till the factories agree to pay higher prices.
They are demanding ₹4,250 a tonne from the sugar factories and ₹1,250 incentive from the State government as State Advised Price.
They said that they will not accept the ₹3,600 per tonne and the profit-sharing formula agreed upon in Belagavi.

They expressed anger against the Union government for failing to revise the Minimum Selling Price of sugar and against the State government for failing to announce SAP. They insisted that sugar factories begin operations only after announcing a higher price.

“Farmers are going around villages, making public announcements urging others not to harvest sugarcane and to join the protest. If the 14 sugar factories in the district begin operations without announcing the price, the factory owners themselves will be held responsible for any untoward incidents that may follow,” farmers leader Eerappa Hanchinal said.
Another leader Sangamesh said that the politicians and factory owners have diluted the protest in Belagavi by dividing farmers and threatening them that delay in crushing will damage their crops.
He also challenged the factories to start crushing operations without the consent of farmers.
Farmers leader Basavantappa said that some factories have not paid last year’s arrears to farmers.

fullParagraphs: Kerala School Science Drama Competition blends performance and scientific thinking to spark curiosity among young minds

articles.title: TGPCB panel calls for action against construction companies over environmental violations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB)’s task force committee has recommended the closure of four construction projects in Hyderabad and Rangareddy districts for carrying out construction activities without obtaining consent for establishment.
It has also recommended the closure of a captive ready mix concrete (RMC) plant operating without consent and adequate pollution control measures.

The recommendations followed inspections by the board’s Rolling Task Force teams in response to complaints of air pollution caused by construction activity. The inspections revealed several violations, including inadequate dust-control measures, improper storage and disposal of construction waste, and excessive noise levels.

The committee reviewed the compliance status of 18 construction projects at a meeting held at the TGPCB head office on Wednesday. Regional Officers, Task Force teams and representatives of the construction projects concerned attended the meeting.

The inspections found that several projects had failed to provide wind-breaking walls of at least 10 metres in height. Dust accumulation on internal roads and surrounding streets, inadequate sprinkling of water, and open storage of sand and construction debris were also reported.

Other violations included improper disposal of construction and demolition (C&D) waste, failure to maintain records of waste disposal, use of MS (Mild Steel) drum chutes instead of HDPE chutes, and ambient noise levels exceeding the prescribed daytime commercial limit of 65 dB(A), a statement from TGPCB informed.

The committee recommended environmental compensation for projects with major violations and forfeiture of bank guarantees in cases involving minor violations. It also directed non-compliant projects to rectify the deficiencies within 10 days, the statement said, without naming the violators.
The committee recommended stoppage of construction activities at another project for non-compliance. The board will initiate further action based on the recommendations.

articles.title: Netanyahu dismisses claims that Israel blocking supplies to Gaza
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Benjamin Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Donald Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected accusations that Israel has been delaying the entry of winter supplies into the Gaza Strip as the enclave faces worsening conditions this week, with severe rains flooding makeshift tents.
He said Israel was not to blame for the worsening conditions for Palestinians in Gaza's tent camps that have been hit by severe winter floods.

His remarks came after the U.S.-created Board of Peace — established under U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Israel-Hamas war and oversee Gaza's recovery — said Monday (November 9, 2026) that Israel's delaying of the entry of winter supplies into Gaza had “exacerbated the consequences of a foreseeable humanitarian challenge”.

Torrential rain has battered the war-torn enclave in recent days, damaging tens of thousands of makeshift tents. Four people, including three children, were killed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) when a large sandstone slab collapsed onto tents during the rains.

Mr. Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Mr. Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes.
“Hamas alone is responsible for the suffering of the people of Gaza, and it is now cynically exploiting that suffering to shift blame onto Israel once again,” he said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the situation in Gaza was “intolerable” and demanded Israel end “arbitrary restrictions” on aid. And in Washington, Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii, the top Democrat on the Senate's foreign spending subcommittee, called for Israel to immediately allow winter gear into Gaza.

“There are a lot of challenges when it comes to Israel and Palestine that are complicated, and fraught, and contentious,” Mr. Schatz said on the Senate floor on Tuesday (November 10, 2026). “But we should all be able to agree that repairing torn tents and helping people to dry out, and providing warmth to freezing children is a basic human obligation.”

Mr. Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Mr. Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes.

“Hamas alone is responsible for the suffering of the people of Gaza, and it is now cynically exploiting that suffering to shift blame onto Israel once again,” he said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the situation in Gaza was “intolerable” and demanded Israel end “arbitrary restrictions” on aid. And in Washington, Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii, the top Democrat on the Senate's foreign spending subcommittee, called for Israel to immediately allow winter gear into Gaza.

“There are a lot of challenges when it comes to Israel and Palestine that are complicated, and fraught, and contentious,” Mr. Schatz said on the Senate floor on Tuesday (November 10, 2026). “But we should all be able to agree that repairing torn tents and helping people to dry out, and providing warmth to freezing children is a basic human obligation.”

articles.title: Central committee suggests three-year roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand mining from active river channels
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: In its report, the CEC observes that while sand and gravel are crucial ingredients for infrastructure and construction, their unscientific or excessive extraction from active channels and floodplains disrupts the delicate dynamic balance of river systems

The Supreme Court-appointed Central Empowered Committee (CEC) has suggested preparing a time-bound roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand extraction from active river channels over the next three years.

The committee, a statutory body since 2023 and originally formed in 2002 on the apex court's order, has also recommended developing sustainable alternative sources of sand and aggregates to progressively reduce dependence on extraction from active river channels.
For this, it has suggested scientific desiltation of dams and reservoirs and recycling of construction and demolition (C&D) waste, among other measures.
These recommendations are part of the CEC's report submitted to the Supreme Court on November 2 as part of a sou motu case related to illegal sand mining in the National Chambal Sanctuary.

In its report, the CEC observes that while sand and gravel are crucial ingredients for infrastructure and construction, their unscientific or excessive extraction from active channels and floodplains disrupts the delicate dynamic balance of river systems.

"The impacts inter alia include riverbed degradation and infrastructure vulnerability, depletion of groundwater and loss of aquifers, destruction of aquatic and riparian habitats, and alteration of river morphology and hydrology, etc," said the committee.
It also highlights that there is no consolidated, reliable national database that quantifies the volume or value of illegally extracted river sand.
As a result, the CEC has recommended strengthening the existing regulatory and monitoring framework governing extraction from permissible areas.

This can be done through scientific identification of mineable stretches, regular replenishment studies, determination of sustainable extraction limits, environmental safeguards, digital tracking of mineral transportation and end-use and effective enforcement, it said.

"A time-bound roadmap shall be prepared to progressively phase out unsustainable sand extraction from active river channels over the next three years, alongside development of adequate alternative sources, including reservoir sediment, M-sand and recycled C&D waste, while ensuring that legitimate construction requirements are met,” the CEC said in its report.

articles.title: Prix Pascal: If AI writes your book, are you still a writer?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: France’s new Prix Pascal for AI-assisted books prompts a writer to reflect on the slow pleasures of making art, loss of individuality, and need to reclaim human imagination

There is now a new French literary prize for AI-assisted writing — the Prix Pascal de Littérature IA. The Pascal prize requires entrants to turn in an unpublished manuscript, fiction or non-fiction, in French, of approximately 3,00,000 characters, written with the help of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Writers must declare which AI model and prompts they have employed. The applications, to be submitted by November 30, consist of “a seed, a manuscript and a technical file, submitted simultaneously”. Ten finalists will be announced on December 4 and the winner will be revealed on December 15.

“This [submitted] work must be useful, or raise awareness, or help to solve in an original way one of the ecological, social and ethical challenges that threaten humanity. AI can now solve previously unsolvable mathematical problems. Here, it is asked to produce a text that will help humanity progress towards wisdom and the preservation of itself and its environment.”

I love the way in which the manifesto strategically reframes tacit support for what goes against the very grain of the creative spirit as an essentially moral and ethical act. But of course! This is the way these things are usually done. The prize was founded by Philippe Rodriguez, Albin Serviant and Gilles Mentré. The first two are technology entrepreneurs, which too is no surprise.

Notwithstanding their precarity, writers and artists have always been viewed with a combination of envy, fear and hatred. The imagination is a dangerous thing. It is ungovernable. It cannot easily be controlled or colonised. It does not seek permission. And that, to many, is frightening. What better way to colonise the imagination than to introduce AI into the writer’s world? Also, that way everybody — even the ones with little understanding of what a writer does — can acquire the overnight label of one. Where does this leave writers who have spent years honing their craft, writers who have survived by the skin of their teeth? The world needs writers more urgently than ever before, and more of us should let some form of creative practice into our lives.

Two semesters ago, a few students from my Creative Writing course, at Shiv Nadar University, Chennai, confessed to what their worst fears were: that, having come of age in the post-AI era, they would find it a challenge to access and exercise their imagination — which, in their understanding, was foundational to the course. I was struck by their capacity for self-reflection, moved by what they recognised, quite rightly, as an imminent loss. This, too, is the other dark side of what we have got ourselves into: the loss of imagination is foundational not just to the stray creative writing course but to life itself.

The argument that it is best not to be left behind, that AI is here to stay so writers must take the good things it has to offer and navigate the rest, is a specious one. The folks making this argument may be right about the inevitability of AI, but does that make any of it less disturbing or a tad more ethical? I don’t see how one can frame this as anything other than a pure black-and-white story. If you give AI an inch, it is very likely that you will take a mile from yourself.

It is a slippery slope. You start by using AI as an instrument — perhaps to help you rewrite a sentence — and before you know it, you are likely to seek its help extensively to write the entire piece. Who then is the real author of the piece? After all, it is in the writing that writers do their thinking. I don’t think the answer lies in declaring AI use upfront. While this may address the ethical question to a small extent, it still does not change the fact that we are always going to ‘writing’ with training wheels on. The craft is in the writing and if you give that away what is left?

There is another problem too: that of the asymmetry between the writer on whose work an LLM is trained and the user who then draws on that work to write in “collaboration with” that particular AI model. The original writer whose consent has very likely not been sought gets nothing from this entire process — a process which de-humanises creative work and repurposes it as training data.

Artificial intelligence illustrations are seen on a lapto with books in the background in this illustration photo on 18 July, 2023. (Photo by Jaap Arriens/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | Photo Credit: Getty Images

As almost everyone from editors of literary journals on the brink of closure to writing teachers will tell you, it is often impossible to tell AI-assisted writing apart from human writing. In fact, you may find that some AI-assisted writing may be as good as if not better than writing by humans. It, of course, depends on the prompts used and how advanced the models are.
